name: Anti-Zionism
summary: Anti-Zionism is opposition to Zionism and to the idea of a Jewish state, held for very different reasons: Bundist, Reform, German-Jewish and Orthodox or Haredi Jews, Israeli Marxists such as Matzpen, groups such as Jewish Voice for Peace, and many Palestinians. The defining sources agree on the rejection of a Jewish state in Palestine and, for the secular left, on calling Zionism settler-colonial and discriminatory; they share no programme on economics, religion, government or most other questions.
scope: Anti-Zionism as the defining sources present it: opposition to Zionism and to a Jewish state, across Jewish (Bundist, Reform, German-Jewish, Orthodox and Haredi, Israeli Marxist) and secular-left currents, using Myers's scholarly survey, Jewish Voice for Peace's own account and Matzpen's The Other Israel. Palestinian nationalist texts such as the 1968 Palestinian National Charter and Said's writings are a different subject's platforms (an organisation's, a thinker's) that no defining source ties to the ideology, so they answer nothing here. Soviet anti-Zionism and Islamist currents are excluded.
